title: Database
description: Query-level performance visible from SQLAlchemy instrumentation. Server-side Postgres metrics (connections, pg_stat_statements, replication lag) are NOT emitted by Phase 5 and are explicitly marked unavailable below rather than faked.

panels.title: Slow queries (p95/p99 duration)
panels.query: approx_percentile_cont(duration, 0.95 | 0.99) over SQLAlchemy query spans (emitted by logfire.instrument_sqlalchemy()), bucketed per minute.
panels.notes: Backed by SQLAlchemy engine-level query spans, not a server-side Postgres exporter.

panels.title: Top statements by total time
panels.query: SQLAlchemy query spans grouped by normalized statement text, summed duration and call count over the selected time range, ordered descending by total time.
panels.notes: This approximates a pg_stat_statements 'top by total time' view using client-side query spans, since no server-side statement-stats exporter is deployed in Phase 5.

panels.title: Query error rate
panels.query: Count of SQLAlchemy query spans with an error/exception status, bucketed per minute, as a proxy for DB-level failures (constraint violations, deadlocks, connection errors surfaced at the query layer).

panels.title: Active connection count
panels.query: Would require a server-side Postgres exporter (e.g. postgres_exporter reading pg_stat_activity) — not shipped in Phase 5.
panels.notes: No signal currently emits this. Requires deploying a Postgres metrics exporter alongside Logfire; out of scope for Phase 5's application-level instrumentation.

panels.title: pg_stat_statements top 10
panels.query: Would require enabling the pg_stat_statements extension and a server-side exporter to surface it to Logfire — not shipped in Phase 5.
panels.notes: The 'Top statements by total time' panel above is the closest available approximation, derived from client-side SQLAlchemy spans rather than server-side statement statistics.

panels.title: Replication lag
panels.query: Would require a server-side Postgres exporter reporting pg_stat_replication / WAL lag — not shipped in Phase 5 (single-primary deployment with no read replica currently, and no exporter regardless).
panels.notes: No signal currently emits this. Add a Postgres exporter and, if/when a replica exists, this panel can be backed.
